answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions depend on a stake locked in a public contract: each identity posts collateral before it can submit work, and validators slash that collateral when a fraud proof shows duplicate or fabricated contributions. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence for free; every account needs its own capital, which is frozen and exposed to loss. A copper ledger may record deposits from dawn onward, while honest agents wander between tasks without risking penalties for merely changing roles.
